articles.title_orig: Obama judge halts Trump firing bid as decades-old legal authority tees up possible major reversal
articles.title_zh: Obama judge halts Trump firing bid as decades-old legal authority tees up possible major reversal
articles.content_orig:
U.S. District Court Judge James Boasberg, who blocked President Donald Trump from deporting hundreds of Venezuelan migrants, is among the judges who have attracted attention from critics. 'Fox News @ Night' takes a closer look.
An Obama-appointed judge blocked President Donald Trump from firing court-appointed U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington Roger Rogoff, ordering the Justice Department to recognize Rogoff as the rightful officeholder and restore his ability to serve.
"This is yet another ruling from an activist judge trying to thwart President Trump’s agenda and undermine his constitutional authority. U.S. attorneys serve at the pleasure of the President," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital.
Judge Stanley Bastian, who was first nominated by Obama in 2013, issued a preliminary injunction reinstating Rogoff and barring the administration from treating him as having been lawfully removed. The ruling sets up a legal fight over whether a president can fire a U.S. attorney appointed by federal judges. A 1979 Justice Department opinion and a 2000 federal appeals court ruling both concluded that the president has that authority.
"We disagree with the decision and intend to seek an immediate stay and will appeal," the DOJ Rapid Response account wrote.
TRUMP ADMIN FIRES US ATTORNEY IN SEATTLE MINUTES AFTER HE WAS APPOINTED
President Donald Trump’s administration secured an interim Supreme Court victory allowing it to continue third-country deportations while the legal battle plays out. (Getty Images)
Some legal experts and conservative attorneys took to social media to sharply criticize the ruling, arguing it infringes on the president's constitutional authority over the executive branch.
"Another lawless and dangerous ruling. Violating the separation of powers. By another Democrat activist judge. This time? Seattle Obama Judge Stanley Bastian," wrote Article III founder and president Mike Davis .
"Democrat judges handpicked their own U.S. attorney. The President, through his attorney general, fired him. Under Article II of the Constitution , the President clearly has the executive power to fire Justice Department officials," Davis added.
Davis also noted Bastian’s first name was misspelled in the order, missing the "e" in Stanley.
'ROGUE' OBAMA JUDGE'S SMACKDOWN OF TRUMP ELECTION RULES PROVOKES OMINOUS WARNING FROM WHITE HOUSE DEPUTY
FILE - The majority of the cuts were aimed at Health and Human Services programs. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
"The Federal Judge misspelled his own name in his order. That's how you know it's quality legal work," wrote one user.
"Now Judge Bastian created an unnecessary constitutional crisis by essentially ordering a coup at the Justice Department, by ordering the removal of the President’s pick and putting in Bastian’s judicial puppet. The Ninth Circuit must fix this. Or the Supreme Court will have to step in. Again," Davis concluded.
"The President's power to remove U.S. Attorneys must be unfettered consistent with Article II of the Constitution. Judge Stanley Bastian is wrong here to order Rogoff reinstated. I predict Judge Bastian will eventually be reversed, whether at the Ninth Circuit or by the Supreme Court," said Oversight Project litigation vice president Jeff Clark .
WHITE HOUSE RIPS ‘ACTIVIST’ BIDEN JUDGE WHO UPENDED TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP ORDER
Justice Department lawyers asked a federal judge Friday to dismiss a lawsuit challenging the Anti-Weaponization Fund, arguing Attorney General Todd Blanche formally terminated it Aug. 2. (Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
"Judicial overreach, plain and simple. The judiciary does not get to run the Executive Branch. Period," said Holtzman Vogel partner Brian Nieves .
In Myers v. United States (1926), which centered on President Woodrow Wilson's firing of a postmaster without Senate consent, the Supreme Court ruled that the president generally has constitutional authority to remove executive branch officers.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
More recently, the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel concluded in a 1979 opinion that the president’s statutory authority to remove "each United States attorney" also extends to prosecutors appointed by federal judges.
The case is the latest in a string of legal fights over President Trump's U.S. attorney appointments, following similar disputes in New Jersey, Virginia and New York.
A similar dispute unfolded in New Jersey after the administration sought to keep Alina Habba leading the U.S. attorney’s office after her interim term ended. Federal courts ultimately rejected the administration’s effort to maintain her authority, although the judges’ original appointee, Desiree Grace, did not simply take over the office.
Rogoff’s case goes a step further, directly testing whether a president can remove a U.S. attorney appointed by federal judges under the statutory process for filling a vacancy.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

Southern California is about to experience at least a week of extreme heat, according to the National Weather Service.
An extreme heat advisory is in effect for many areas from 10 a.m. Friday through 8 p.m. Thursday and may be extended. People are advised to remain hydrated, avoid the sun, stay in an air-conditioned room and check on loved ones.
A strong high-pressure system will set up over the eastern Pacific and West Coast starting Friday and will increase through Sunday, sending temperatures 15 to 20 degrees above normal, the weather service said.
That means when the Dodgers and Atlanta Braves take the field Saturday for the National League Division Series, it could be as hot as 95 degrees on the field.

However, tropical moisture is expected to enter the area by next weekend, which could lead to some cooling, according to the weather service.

articles.title_orig: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.title_zh: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.content_orig:
Long-term data reinforce durable efficacy and safety of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in late-onset Pompe disease
BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc . (Nasdaq: BMRN ) today announced new data evaluating the efficacy and safety of POMBILITI® (cipaglucosidase alfa-atga) + OPFOLDA® (miglustat) in late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) were presented at the 31st Annual Congress of the World Muscle Society (WMS), in Hiroshima, Japan.
These results from the PROPEL open-label extension (OLE) study of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, which were shared in a late-breaking presentation, demonstrated durable motor function outcomes and relative stabilization of pulmonary function over long-term follow-up. The analysis included data from 82 individuals who received POMBILITI + OPFOLDA continuously from baseline observed in the initial PROPEL study (PROPEL baseline) to year five. For the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)-experienced cohort, the mean duration of prior ERT at baseline was 7.6 years. These data represent long-term benefits for people with LOPD followed in the study, including both ERT-experienced and ERT-naïve cohorts.
"These five-year results demonstrate that POMBILITI and OPFOLDA can provide durable, long-term benefits for people living with late-onset Pompe disease, including those who had been on enzyme replacement therapy for years before enrolling in the study," said Greg Friberg, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Research & Development Officer at BioMarin. "Sustaining motor function and limiting pulmonary decline for up to five years in a progressive disease like LOPD is clinically meaningful, and we remain committed to continuing to share long-term evidence to inform the care of people with this rare genetic condition."
Table 1. Efficacy Measures With POMBILITI + OPFOLDA From PROPEL Baseline (BL) for up to Five Years
Mean (standard deviation, SD) change from baseline in % predicted six-minute walk distance (pp6MWD)
Mean (SD) change from baseline in % predicted forced vital capacity (ppFVC)
No new safety signals were identified. 51.2% of participants (n=42) experienced treatment-related adverse events, the majority of which were manageable. Five individuals discontinued treatment for safety reasons, including two due to serious treatment-related adverse events (chills and hypoxia [n=1], anaphylactoid reaction [n=1]).
Phase 1/2 Data Show Positive Dystrophin Expression and Favorable Tolerability With Nivudirsen (BMN 351)
Additional presentations at WMS included data evaluating nivudirsen (BMN 351), an investigational antisense oligonucleotide for ambulatory boys ages 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. Included in these presentations was an update from the ongoing Phase 1/2 351-201 study, which was previously shared at the 19th International Congress on Neuromuscular Diseases in July. Results from 351-201 showed treatment with nivudirsen was generally well tolerated and led to consistently positive outcomes across multiple measures of therapeutic benefit, including expression of near full-length dystrophin.
Below are key presentations at WMS, with all times listed in Japan Standard Time:
Phase 1/2 Results of BMN 351, an Antisense Oligonucleotide for Exon 51 Skip-Amenable Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Poster Presentation #2.66P Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Comprehensive Panel of Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic and Biomarker Measures Drives Clinical Development of BMN 351 for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy E-Poster Presentation #2.43eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.

Long-Term (Five-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline E-Poster Presentation #3.081LBeP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Four-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline Poster Presentation #3.56P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Baseline Disease Burden and Real-World Monitoring Practices: Global Insights From the followME Pompe Journey Registry Poster Presentation #3.57P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.

About the PROPEL Open-Label Extension Study
The Phase 3 open-label extension (OLE) study (ATB200-07; NCT04138277 ) is a multicenter, international study designed to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in adults with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) who completed the Phase 3 PROPEL study (ATB200-03; NCT03729362 ). Of the 118 people treated in the OLE, 82 continued POMBILITI + OPFOLDA treatment from PROPEL (62 ERT-experienced prior to PROPEL; 20 ERT-naïve) and 37 switched from the comparator arm to POMBILITI + OPFOLDA (29 ERT-experienced; eight ERT-naïve).
The study evaluates long-term changes from PROPEL baseline in six-minute walk distance (6MWD, the primary endpoint in PROPEL), forced vital capacity (FVC), creatine kinase (CK) and hexose tetrasaccharide (Hex4) levels, and patient-reported outcomes, as well as long-term safety.
The 351-201 trial ( NCT06280209 ) is a Phase 1/2 multicenter open-label dose-escalation study evaluating BMN 351 for the treatment of boys aged 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy with a specific genetic change amenable to exon 51 skipping. The primary endpoints examine the safety and tolerability of BMN 351, the secondary endpoints assess plasma, urine and muscle pharmacokinetics, and key exploratory endpoints include exon-skipping efficiency, dystrophin expression, immunogenicity and functional assessments.
The study is being conducted in three cohorts, with Cohort 1 being divided into Cohort 1A and Cohort 1B. In Cohort 1A, three boys received increasing doses once every two weeks with a visit to assess safety measures collected the week after dosing prior to escalating doses of BMN 351. In part two, the participants in Cohort 1A transitioned to once-weekly dosing. The participants in Cohort 1B, 2 and 3 will receive low (6 mg/kg), medium (9 mg/kg) and high (12 mg/kg) doses of BMN 351 and continue once-weekly dosing at that same dose.
For more information, please visit clinicaltrials.biomarin.com .
About Late-Onset Pompe Disease
Late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) is an inherited lysosomal disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA). Reduced or absent levels of GAA lead to accumulation of glycogen in cells, which is believed to result in the clinical manifestations of Pompe disease. LOPD can be severe and debilitating with progressive muscle weakness throughout the body that worsens over time, particularly in skeletal muscles and muscles that control breathing.
About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe neuromuscular condition that leads to progressive muscle weakness and premature mortality. DMD is caused by genetic changes that result in the absence or dysfunction of dystrophin, an essential protein that is necessary for preserving muscle function.
As an X-linked disorder, DMD primarily affects young boys, with onset of symptoms occurring around 2 to 3 years of age. The incidence of DMD is up to 1 in 3,600 to 6,000 live male births.
Individuals with DMD experience serious functional impairments, including loss of limb strength and ambulation, and respiratory and cardiovascular impacts that require lifelong care.
POMBILITI + OPFOLDA is a two-component therapy that consists of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga, a bis-M6P-enriched rhGAA that facilitates high-affinity uptake through the M6P receptor while retaining its capacity for processing into the most active form of the enzyme, and the oral enzyme stabilizer

articles.title_orig: Look up: Saturn is at its brightest this weekend
articles.title_zh: Look up: Saturn is at its brightest this weekend
articles.content_orig:
Saturn is at its biggest and brightest as the ringed planet reaches opposition this weekend.
Opposition happens as Earth passes between Saturn and the Sun, bringing the planet to its closest point to Earth for the year, about 784 million miles (1.26 billion km) away. This minimum distance makes Saturn appear brighter than at any other time this year.
Opposition is a great time to observe Saturn because it rises in the east around sunset, reaches its highest point around midnight, and remains visible through dawn. It will appear as a yellowish point of light in the eastern and southeastern sky.
You do not need a telescope to see Saturn, but even a small telescope can reveal the planet's rings and the brightest couple of its 293 moons. While you are spotting Saturn, look a bit higher for a large grouping of four stars astronomers call the Great Square of Pegasus. Up and to the right is the Circlet (ring) of Pisces. These are asterisms, or recognizable patterns within the more official constellations of Pegasus (the winged horse) and Pisces (the fish).
2026's view is very different from last year's when Earth crossed the plane of Saturn’s rings. Though the ring system spans about 175,000 miles, it is, on average, about 30 feet thick, so it effectively disappears when viewed edge-on. Since opposition in 2025, the rings are tilted 7.5 degrees from our perspective, bringing them back into view.
Saturn will be at opposition on Sunday morning at 8:21 a.m., but with clouds expected this weekend, the best views will be tonight, Friday, Oct. 2. The planet will remain an excellent evening target for much of the month.
Saturn’s last opposition occurred Sept. 21, 2025. Saturn reaches opposition every 378 days, or about two weeks later each year, as Earth catches up with Saturn in its orbit. We'll have similar good opportunities to view Jupiter as it reaches its own opposition on Feb. 11, 2027, followed by Mars on Feb. 19, 2027.

articles.title_orig: NFCB Names Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett Co-Directors
articles.title_zh: NFCB Names Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett Co-Directors
articles.content_orig:
Update your browser to view this website correctly. Update my browser now
Home › News and Business › People News
The National Federation of Community Broadcasters has announced that Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett will serve as co-directors starting next year, while Rima Dael will conclude her service as CEO.
Mead, NFCB’s director of member engagement, and Aston-Puckett, its chief operating officer, bring around four decades of combined nonprofit and community media experience, including work at KZMU(FM) in Utah and KVNF(FM) in Colorado.
The change is effective Jan. 1. With the move, Rima Dael will conclude her service as the organization’s CEO at the end of December as the association moves to a two-person permanent staff. The nonprofit has a nine-person board of directors.
[Related: “Future in Focus: Rima Dael of the NFCB”]
Dael supported the structural change and is helping lead the transition, according to NFCB. She has not accepted another position. The organization’s board credited Dael’s leadership in strengthening fundraising, research, partnerships and national advocacy.
According to a release, the change follows board and staff planning in response to the loss of Corporation for Public Broadcasting support. NFCB said it is aligning its expenses with membership revenue while keeping assistance, training, regulatory guidance, resources and peer connections as its focus.
NFCB received a $1.25 million general operating grant from the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation in 2025. It is investing in member resources including rural audience research, an updated legal handbook, emergency preparedness tools and station training.
The National Federation of Community Broadcasters has been serving the nation’s community radio stations since 1978.

articles.title_orig: Officials Say NVIDIA Missed Red Flags in China Chip Smuggling Cases
articles.title_zh: Officials Say NVIDIA Missed Red Flags in China Chip Smuggling Cases
articles.content_orig:
Federal prosecutors have charged a man with illegally shipping NVIDIA artificial intelligence chips to China, Bloomberg reported on Oct. 2.
Government officials told Bloomberg in a feature published Oct. 1 that NVIDIA is not doing enough to stop the trade. NVIDIA has never been accused of helping smugglers. It says it has followed the rules.
The Justice Department announced the arrest of Greg Lui on Oct. 1. He is accused of smuggling servers holding $300 million worth of AI chips to China in violation of US export laws.
Earlier this year, officials released surveillance video. It shows a person using a red hair dryer to peel serial number stickers off NVIDIA server boxes.
Bloomberg cited one warning sign. Thailand and Singapore, both next to China, were receiving more chips than they could use. Daniel Remler, a former State Department AI policy head, said he never received a straight answer.
His question was how so many chips could flow to Southeast Asia if they were not serving Chinese customers.
Bloomberg also reported that operators in western China were building dozens of data centers able to house 115,000 restricted NVIDIA processors. Its sources said US officials now believe China has smuggled at least that many chips.
The accused collaborators in one case include Yih-Shyan Liaw, a co-founder of Super Micro. They allegedly sold about $2.5 billion worth of AI servers to OBON, a Bangkok-based company that was supposedly building AI infrastructure in Thailand.
Instead, the servers went straight to end users in China. To get past compliance officers, the conspirators allegedly peeled stickers from genuine NVIDIA products with a hair dryer and attached them to dummy servers.
Officials told Bloomberg that NVIDIA should have noticed OBON lacked the 100 megawatts of data center space needed to host that many servers. Thailand has only a few hundred megawatts of AI data center capacity running. Such a build would have drawn attention.
NVIDIA disputes that view. A spokesperson said a startup's growth plan in a friendly country is an opportunity for America, not a red flag.
The spokesperson said NVIDIA-powered servers are financeable assets that help startups secure capital and infrastructure, including data center space. American companies, the spokesperson added, honor US laws as written.
The company also said progress by Huawei in AI chips means Chinese buyers have no need to smuggle in NVIDIA hardware.
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has lobbied US officials to ease export curbs on China and other Asian nations. Last year, the Trump administration agreed to allow sales of NVIDIA's previous-generation Hopper H200 accelerators to China.
I cover what the internet is actually talking about: the new release, the viral moment, the creator beef, the product launch. My job is to explain it fast and clearly, without the breathless hype. I read the timeline…

articles.title_orig: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Named to TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars List
articles.title_zh: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Named to TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars List
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) this week was named to the TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars list. Senator Britt is the only Republican lawmaker and the only Alabamian named to this year’s list. She is just the second Alabamian ever to receive the honor.
The announcement from TIME can be read below:
“Senator Katie Britt has quickly learned how to wield influence in Donald Trump’s Republican Party while avoiding its hardest edges.
“Not long after she became in 2022 the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the Senate, Mitch McConnell invited her to join his weekly leadership meetings as an adviser, giving her access to the GOP’s longtime power center.
“Britt, 44, has since strongly backed Trump’s agenda, including his aggressive immigration policies, while privately urging the Administration toward moderation at key moments.
“The Alabama lawmaker has also carved out her own policy lane around families and children. Britt pressed Trump to protect IVF after an Alabama court ruling threatened access to the procedure, helped secure expanded childcare tax credits, and has worked across the aisle on legislation protecting children from social media. Her ability to bridge divides within the GOP while cultivating bipartisan relationships has made Britt an increasingly consequential player in the Senate.”
Senator Britt released the following statement in response to the honor:
“I’m deeply humbled by this recognition, but it truly belongs to the people of Alabama. Every single day, I’m focused on making sure the hardworking families in our state and across our nation have the opportunity to thrive — whether that’s making childcare more affordable and accessible, ensuring continued nationwide access to IVF, keeping our nation safe and secure, or protecting our kids online. Serving Alabama is the honor of a lifetime, and I’ll keep fighting day in and day out to put the people I represent in a stronger place as a result of my service.”

articles.title_orig: Looking to expand in China? iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 connects global suppliers with Chinese buyers
articles.title_zh: Looking to expand in China? iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 connects global suppliers with Chinese buyers
articles.content_orig:
The 19th iFresh Asia Fruit Expo will take place from November 4–6, 2026, at Hangzhou International Expo Center Phase II in Hangzhou, China, bringing together more than 500 exhibitors and 8,000 professional visitors across the fresh produce value chain.
For international fruit companies looking to enter or expand in China, finding an importer is only the beginning.
China has a large and rapidly evolving fresh produce market, with channels ranging from wholesale markets, fruit retail chains and supermarkets to e-commerce platforms, premium fruit stores and emerging retail formats. Each channel has different requirements when it comes to varieties, quality, specifications, packaging, pricing, and supply consistency.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
Which products are Chinese buyers looking for? Which channels offer new opportunities for imported fruit? How can international suppliers find the right partners? And what trends are shaping China’s fruit market today?
These are some of the questions that international companies will have the opportunity to explore at iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 , taking place from November 4–6 in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China .
For companies seeking more Chinese buyers, new distribution channels, reliable local partners, and a better understanding of the latest developments in China’s fruit market , Hangzhou will provide three days of concentrated access to the industry.
The 2026 edition of iFresh Asia Fruit Expo will cover approximately 20,000 square meters , bringing together 500+ exhibitors and 8,000 professional visitors .
The exhibition spans the fruit industry value chain, from seedlings, fresh produce, and fruit brands to processed fruit products, post-harvest technology, preservation, sorting, packaging, and cold-chain logistics.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
Six dedicated exhibition areas will showcase different segments of the industry:
Fresh Fruit & Brand Zone | International Fruit Zone | Technology & Supply Chain Zone | Fruit Processing Zone | Fruit Channel Food Zone | Organic Food Brand Zone
For international suppliers, participating in iFresh is not simply about displaying products. It is an opportunity to meet potential partners from different parts of China’s fruit distribution and supply chain ecosystem in one place.
Whether a company wants to introduce fresh fruit to China, identify importers and distributors, explore new retail channels, or discover solutions in preservation, sorting, packaging, and cold-chain logistics, the expo is designed to provide direct access to relevant industry resources.
For B2B exhibitors, the number of contacts collected at a trade show matters less than whether those contacts lead to real business opportunities.
That is why business matchmaking will be a major focus of this year’s iFresh Asia Fruit Expo.
Hangzhou is widely recognized as one of China’s leading e-commerce hubs and is located in the Yangtze River Delta, one of the country’s most economically active consumer markets.
Against this backdrop, the expo will bring together professional buyers and decision-makers from wholesale markets, fruit retail chains, supermarkets, e-commerce platforms, new retail businesses, supply chain companies, and other distribution channels .
Dedicated Fresh Fruit & Fruit Channel Food Business Matchmaking Sessions will also take place during the exhibition, alongside the “100 Counties, 100 Products” Roadshow & Matchmaking Program .
These activities are designed to bring suppliers closer to buyers with actual sourcing needs, creating more focused opportunities for face-to-face business discussions.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
For companies entering China for the first time, this is also an opportunity to hear directly from Chinese buyers about what they are looking for — from product quality and specifications to packaging, pricing, and supply requirements.
For international brands and suppliers already active in China, the iFresh Asia Fruit Expo offers a chance to explore additional channels, regional markets and potential new partners.
One new feature of this year’s exhibition is the dedicated Fruit Channel Food Zone , reflecting changes taking place across China’s fruit retail sector.
A growing number of fruit retailers in China are expanding beyond fresh produce and introducing products such as dried fruit, fruit snacks, juices and other complementary food categories.
For retailers, these products can help broaden their product mix, extend shelf life, create more consumption occasions and generate additional revenue beyond fresh fruit sales.
For international suppliers, this means opportunities within China’s fruit retail channels are no longer limited to fresh produce.
Global fruit processors, snack brands and food companies with products suitable for fruit retail environments can also use the expo to connect with Chinese fruit chains, retailers, distributors and professional buyers.
Entering a market is not only about finding customers. It is also about understanding where the market is heading.
Alongside the exhibition, iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 will host a series of industry conferences under the Fruit Elite Island program, covering key topics currently being discussed across China’s fruit industry.
The conference program includes:
The sessions will bring together industry professionals and business representatives to discuss developments across fruit growing, retail, branding, wholesale and distribution, processing, organic food and emerging business models .
For international companies, the value goes beyond attending a conference.
Companies that want to build a long-term presence in China need to understand what Chinese buyers are discussing, how distribution channels are changing, what retailers are looking for, and where new consumer and product opportunities are emerging .
Through three days of exhibitions, matchmaking, and industry discussions, overseas participants can gain a closer look at the dynamics shaping China’s fruit business.
China offers significant opportunities, but building a sustainable business in the market requires more than simply bringing a product into the country.
Finding the right buyers, understanding channel requirements, developing local partnerships, and keeping pace with market changes are all essential.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
If you are looking for more Chinese buyers, if you want to expand your distribution network in China, if you are searching for importers, distributors or long-term business partners, or if you want a closer look at the latest trends shaping China’s fruit market,
iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 is an opportunity to connect with the market face-to-face.
From product showcases and targeted buyer matchmaking to industry insights and full supply-chain connections, the three-day event aims to create practical business opportunities between international suppliers and China’s fruit industry.

articles.title_orig: 5 European nations follow U.S. with plans for third-country deportations as EU approves migrant "return hubs"
articles.title_zh: 5 European nations follow U.S. with plans for third-country deportations as EU approves migrant "return hubs"
articles.content_orig:
Five European Union countries are pushing ahead with plans to start deporting asylum seekers whose applications are rejected to third countries outside the bloc, potentially in Africa, after the EU approved new rules this week that clear the way for the practice.
Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands have agreed on a common framework to establish "return hubs" outside the EU to which people who have exhausted their legal options to remain in Europe could be transferred if they cannot be sent back to their own countries of origin.
"When it comes to return hubs, it's progressing very well," Danish Interior Minister Morten Bødskov told reporters Thursday, according to AFP . "We are moving in the right direction."
He previously said Denmark expected "to be ready to transfer the first irregular migrants to a partner country outside the EU within 2027."
Greek Migration Minister Thanos Plevris told Politico that Greece expects to have a pilot project in place in the first half of next year.
No potential destinations for EU return hubs have been confirmed, although Rwanda has been reported as a possible partner in the project. A Greek government statement on the plans said the hubs would be established in safe third countries, "particularly on the African continent."
The EU itself has presented the idea of return hubs as a potential deterrent to irregular immigration. A discussion paper published by the EU's governing European Council in October 2025 said the hubs could "incentivize voluntary returns," because migrants who fail to comply with a deportation order could face transfer to a hub instead.
It said the policy could also discourage people without a valid asylum claim from making dangerous journeys to Europe.
The rules adopted this week by the EU establish a bloc-wide legal framework for returns and allow member states to conclude bilateral or unilateral agreements with countries outside the bloc, but with stipulations.
Under the rules, "any such agreement or arrangement may only be concluded with a non-EU country that respects international human rights standards and principles of international law, including the principle of non-refoulement ," which guarantees that no individual can be sent back to a country where they would face torture, cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, punishment or other irreparable harm.
The Trump administration has enthusiastically embraced the use of third-country deportations to remove undocumented migrants from the United States. More than 100 deportees were sent to eight African countries over a 10-day period in August, according to internal U.S. government documents obtained by CBS News .
The deportees were sent to destinations including the African nations of Liberia, Rwanda, Eswatini and Sierra Leone.
Plevris, Greece's migration minister, has praised the Trump administration's approach.
"I am a fan of President Trump," he told Breitbart in August. "But if you ask me what was the best thing he did, it was change the migration policy of the USA, because now we have a new migration policy also in Europe."
Other European governments have experimented with deportations to third nations before, however, with mixed results.
Britain's former Conservative Party government sought to send asylum seekers who arrived through irregular routes to Rwanda to have their claims processed there. The U.K. Supreme Court ruled the scheme unlawful in 2023, before it ever got going, over the risk that refugees could ultimately be returned to countries where they faced persecution.
The following year, the policy was formally abandoned by the new Labour Party government after the Conservatives were voted out of power. The British Home Office said £715 million (almost $950 million) had been spent on the Rwanda program by June 2024, and no asylum seekers were forcibly relocated. Four people traveled voluntarily to Rwanda under the program.
"One lesson may be that European governments should expect litigation, even where the third country looks considerably less controversial than Rwanda," Peter Walsh, a senior researcher at the University of Oxford's Migration Observatory, told CBS News on Friday.
"These policies are often justified as deterrence measures, and that assumes a sufficiently large share of people believe there is a realistic chance they will actually be transferred," Walsh said. "If only a very small proportion can be moved, the deterrent may be much less credible."
"The broader lesson from Rwanda is that externalization is not a shortcut around the difficult parts of migration policy," he said. "It may relocate some of those difficulties geographically, but governments still have to deal with courts, individual rights, administrative capacity, countries that may not cooperate with returns, and substantial costs"
The push for return hubs is part of a broader effort by European nations to tighten their immigration policies amid intense pressure on governments to increase the number of people without a legal right to remain who are actually removed.
Jacob Reynolds, policy director at the Freedom and Sovereignty Initiative Europe, a right-wing think tank based in Brussels, called the EU decision to embrace these hubs a "welcome step towards gaining control of our borders and removing those who have no right to be here."
But he added that "outsourcing the problem of illegal migration to third countries — as the EU has long done — risks avoiding the broader problem: the lack of control over EU countries' borders."
He called for "much more fundamental action" to address "the generous regimes available to asylum seekers in Europe," and said until that happened, "the problem will not be solved."

articles.title_orig: Funding Shortages Threaten World Heritage Sites
articles.title_zh: Funding Shortages Threaten World Heritage Sites
articles.content_orig:
By providing your information, you agree to our Terms of Use and our Privacy Policy .
				We use vendors that may also process your information to help provide our services.
The World Monuments Fund (WMF), an independent organization, has warned that funding constraints, intensifying climate change, and a lack of access to expertise are putting World Heritage Sites at extreme risk.
The information comes from WMF’s review of 372 nominations submitted by the public from around the globe as research for the upcoming biannual World Monuments Watch (WMW) list, which will be announced in February. According to the findings, eighty-six percent of nominators cited “funding shortages and economic development” as a primary issue, an increase of 6 percent from last year. Simultaneously, 63 percent identified “opportunities to leverage heritage to support local economies through sustainable tourism, job creation, and urban regeneration.”
“This year’s nominations show that the pressures on heritage are intensifying while the resources to protect it are not keeping pace,” Bénédicte de Montlaur, WMF president and CEO, said in a press release. “According to findings in the UNESCO Global Report on Cultural Policies, only one in four countries has the means to safeguard its heritage.”
Sixty-six percent of nominators cited climate hazards as another major concern, and 30 percent said sites were directly threatened by extreme weather events, flooding, storms, drought, and wildfires. Climate impacts are most severe in sub-Saharan Africa, where 86 percent of sites are under threat. At the same time, the need for technical expertise is increasing, yet 35 percent of nominators identified a “severe lack” of local preservation expertise. In Ghana, for instance, the ten shrines of the Asante Traditional Buildings are endangered as traditional stewardship by master craftspeople declines.
Brinda Somaya, an architect and chair of the WMW International Expert Panel, emphasized the urgency of addressing these risks. “Protecting these sites is vital for preserving local memory, fostering economic resilience, and supporting the communities tied to these places,” she said.

articles.title_orig: France debt crisis: Investors render a ‘guilty’ verdict and are pricing in growing odds of default
articles.title_zh: France debt crisis: Investors render a ‘guilty’ verdict and are pricing in growing odds of default
articles.content_orig:
Faced with the prospect of a far-right or a far-left president, the bond market doesn’t see France curbing its rapidly growing pile of debt anytime soon and has started weighing the possibility that the eurozone’s second largest economy could default.
That’s according to Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie Group. In a note Thursday, he said the cost of insurance against a French default is now the highest among the major EU countries and the U.K.
Early Friday, the signals sharpened further as France’s five-year sovereign credit default swap rose to 81 basis points. At the same time, its 10-year bond yields jumped to 4.989%, the highest since 2002, and the premium over equivalent German yields widened to 152 basis points, the most since the eurozone debt crisis in 2011.
Wizman warned: “The signal from France CDS pricing is that the OAT/Bund spread widening is due to higher sovereign default risk in France.”
Those metrics later came off their highs, but France’s fundamentals remain troubling, with anemic GDP growth, a budget deficit estimated at about 5.4% of GDP, and rising debt-service costs as yields jump.
Meanwhile, France’s debt-to-GDP ratio is expected to climb to 122% next year from 119% this year, and the government’s latest plan failed to halt the surge in bond yields as investors doubted its credibility.
“But our instinct is to also read the suddenly widening OAT/Bund yield spread as a ‘guilty’ verdict on the recent direction of France’s presidential politics,” Wizman wrote. “The problem in particular is political polarization, which has arisen—as it has across Europe—mainly over the immigration issue, rather than fiscal issues. But in France, neither the populist Left nor the populist Right are fiscal hawks.”
Indeed, far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is campaigning on a plan to have the central bank simply cancel its holdings of French debt .
And far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who is leading in the polls for the presidential race, has proposed tax cuts and vowed to bring down France’s retirement age to as low as 60, despite the already generous pension system eating up an ever bigger slice of the budget.
A runoff between the two candidates is expected next year, and Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party is seen as the likely winner.
“As such, an outright default may be a low-probability event, but an RN-led presidency, with an adverse influence on the 2028 budget and credit-risk perceptions is a high-probability event, near 50%,” Wizman added.
He also pointed out that the presidential campaigns have barely begun, meaning the rhetoric around France’s debt, a potential default, and budgetary politics is set to heat up and further damage the perception of the government’s creditworthiness.
To be sure, France isn’t alone in facing high debt and market pressure on its bonds. The U.S. debt-to-GDP ratio is now 100%, and Japan’s is well above 200%.
But America’s GDP growth is much more robust, and Japan enjoys a large pool of built-in demand for its debt from domestic investors. By contrast France’s economy is projected to grow just 0.5% this year, and the government plans to issue over $380 billion in medium- and long-term debt next year.
Ales Koutny, head of international rates at Vanguard, told the Financial Times that demand for debt in markets that become the center of geopolitical issues “can disappear in times of crisis,” describing France as “long-term degrading credit.”
Similarly, Scope Ratings also flagged political risks when it cut France’s credit score to A+ from AA- last month, bringing it on par with Fitch and S&P Global Ratings.
In particular, the ratings firm cited the government’s difficulties in meeting self-imposed deficit targets, adding that the sharp rise in bond yields this year will further increase borrowing costs and make any debt solution even more painful.
“Scope expects political fragmentation to remain elevated beyond the 2027 presidential election, complicating the substantial fiscal consolidation required to stabilize public debt and increasing the risk that measures are diluted, delayed, or only partially implemented over coming years,” it warned. “This weakens Scope’s confidence in France’s ability to halt, let alone reverse, the deterioration of its public finances over the medium term.”
Jason Ma is the weekend editor at Fortune , where he covers markets, the economy, finance, and housing.

articles.title_orig: The gambling world at war
articles.title_zh: The gambling world at war
articles.content_orig:
This week’s annual G2e conference in Las Vegas opened with American Gaming Association CEO Bill Miller telling the main stage audience his organization is “operating on war-time footing” in response to the wildfire growth of prediction market betting.
Miller’s opening was followed by more prediction talk during a “state of gaming” panel featuring MGM CEO Bill Hornbuckle, Caesars CEO Tom Reeg and Wynn CEO Craig Billings.
InGame’s Jill Dorson has G2e coverage here and more here .
Prediction markets have hit a cold streak in the courts of late, losing an appellate decision last week in the 6th Circuit, home to Ohio and Tennessee. That followed a loss in the 9th Circuit, which includes California, Nevada and Arizona, the last of which intends to push for a shutdown . The 4th Circuit is considering a case stemming from attempts to shut Kalshi down in Maryland.
There also was movement in New York, where the state sued Polymarket for running an illegal gambling operation. It took similar action against Kalshi in July.
As a practical matter, actions taken in legalized sports betting states will have less impact than those taken in populous states that haven’t legalized, since the latter is the unplowed land on which operators are competing for new customers. None of those states have moved against Kalshi since the rulings.
The other important development was on the regulatory front, where the CFTC proposed rule changes that would close a loophole that might have allowed for contracts around casino games such as blackjack and roulette, reinforced the Trump administration’s core argument that event contracts are swaps.

articles.title_orig: WebRTC Has Been a Boon
articles.title_zh: WebRTC Has Been a Boon
articles.content_orig:
Update your browser to view this website correctly. Update my browser now
Home › News and Business › News Makers
This is one in a series about how stations are creating and managing their audio from anywhere, thanks to virtualization, cloud, IP and other technologies. This is from the free ebook “ Audio Production (From Anywhere) .”
Jeff McGinley is vice president of engineering at SummitMedia . He says the company approaches distributed workflows in several ways.
“We have a remote morning show co-anchor in another state who uses a traditional codec to dial back into the station every weekday morning — tried and true and well-tested tech that’s been around forever,” he said.
“In three of our markets, we’ve upgraded studios to the Axia Altus console, which has a webRTC backend that allows any computer to act as if it’s a hardware codec.”
SummitMedia also has a remote studio in Gatlinburg, Tenn., located in a restaurant. It is used every week to dial back into the Knoxville stations for a live broadcast.
“Finally, we use the RCS Zetta2Go remote application if we have staff go to do a more traditional appearance remote. Our jocks can record a break on their phone a few minutes before the break is supposed to air. It gets sent to that market’s server, ingested and then played out as ‘almost-live.’”
For McGinley, the introduction of webRTC was crucial.
[Related: “The Stream Is as Important as the Transmitter”]
“This technology is going to change quite a bit in the next few years, and absolutely was not something that was available or at least on most people’s radar five to 10 years ago,” he said.
“Anyone with a laptop can connect via a VPN to the station network and broadcast from anywhere using a very basic setup. I believe that this is going to affect more than just broadcasting from anywhere, but how companies look at real estate and actual studio space,” he said.
“There is no need for a full-sized studio that requires HVAC and sound dampening. Anyone from anywhere with a decent mic and processor can be anywhere in the world and send audio back to get on the air, be it live for a specific on-air show or record a production bit for a commercial for a client.”
Can a complex multi-host morning show be executed as easily and smoothly via a distributed architecture as the traditional single-site installation?
“Absolutely. We are currently doing it with a traditional Comrex codec with a morning show that originates in Omaha but is distributed to almost 50 radio stations,” McGinley replied.
“One of our hosts moved to Pennsylvania, which is when we started doing this. However, this technology has been around for quite a bit now. I set up something similar with a morning show in Audacy in Seattle.”
The main concern, he said, is making the show sound like everyone is still in the same room.
“Kevin and Bean did this for years on KROQ-FM. The back-and-forth banter of the hosts that makes the show work needs to be paramount, even if they’re over 1,100 miles away from each other.”
Investing in IT infrastructure should be the first thing a company tackles when planning such an arrangement.
“On the top of your list should be a top-tier firewall, VPN tunnels and people who understand how to configure and maintain it. This is not something to skimp on.
“Thankfully at SummitMedia, we have the best IT person I’ve ever worked with, Brett Glover. All the credit needs to go to him. He is an absolute wizard at keeping everything running smoothly, keeping all of our VPN tunnels up and running. We also have a number of STLs through what Brett has accomplished.”
McGinley recommends that you conduct frequent penetration testing and educate staff through videos, emails and guidance about when to report suspicious material.
Looking ahead, “There is technology coming that will have both the automation system and a virtual console that will be cloud-based,” he said.
“There are still some considerations that haven’t been answered, like how satellite content delivery and closures will be addressed, but this will definitely be something that we broadcast engineers will have to get ready to deploy in the next few years.
“A wise man I know once said, ‘Wake up and smell the radio.’ Stay tuned. It’s only going to accelerate from here.”

articles.title_orig: NASA Has Been So Thoroughly Screwed by Boeing's Disastrous Starliner That It's Now Throwing Its Entire Access to Space Into Question
articles.title_zh: NASA Has Been So Thoroughly Screwed by Boeing's Disastrous Starliner That It's Now Throwing Its Entire Access to Space Into Question
articles.content_orig:
By all accounts, Boeing’s Starliner spacecraft has been nothing short of a disaster . It’s cost NASA a staggering amount of money, and even after over a decade of development, the capsule still has yet to complete a crewed mission to the International Space Station.
It’s been a humiliating saga, including a failed uncrewed launch attempt that went haywire thanks to a glitching computer, an aborted mission which stranded two NASA astronauts on board the station for nine months, and a litany of technical headaches along the way.
But now that SpaceX is threatening to retire its Crew Dragon spacecraft, NASA could soon be forced to make the plagued spacecraft work whether it likes to or not — while also calling into question its entire access to space.
“I do not think it’s a secret that SpaceX intends to sunset older platforms like Falcon and Dragon as they concentrate on their next-generation capability, Starship,” NASA administrator Jared Isaacman told reporters on Monday.
The agency said that it was weighing the option of buying two additional launches on Boeing’s Starliner.
Without SpaceX’s workhorse Crew Dragon spacecraft, which has regularly delivered crews to the ISS for six years now, NASA’s options could soon run thin. Starliner, which has cost Boeing billions of dollars, came eerily close to getting the axe altogether in 2024, but with SpaceX threatening to abandon its existing launch platforms in favor of its enormous and still unproven Starship, the space agency seemingly saw the writing on the wall.
NASA is also now stuck with the bill. The agency announced this week that it will commit $359 million to bail out Boeing and help it rebuild its reaction control system thrusters, arguably the biggest source of the spacecraft’s woes during its last, ill-fated mission.
The space agency will also need to certify the United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket for crewed missions ahead of the retirement of the Atlas V.
The goal is to launch Starliner no earlier than December of this year. NASA also already has three pre-existing contracts for crewed missions with Boeing, per Ars Technica .
“We are starting with an uncrewed Starliner-1 mission to the International Space Station to validate the improvements made to the spacecraft and gather the flight data we need,” Isaacman said in a statement . “From there, we will use what we learn, continue implementing the corrective actions identified by our Program Investigation Team, and complete the testing and certification required for crewed flight.”
“Our current plan is to return astronauts on Starliner-2 by 2028,” he added.
It’s an awkward transitional moment for the agency. The ISS is set to be retired by the end of this decade, leaving a glaring hole in access to our planet’s orbit. It’s still unclear what will eventually replace the aging orbital outpost, with multiple private companies vying for lucrative government contracts to launch their own habitats.
If it were up to NASA, Boeing’s Starliner would probably be part of that vision — but given what we’ve seen so far, it’s anything but guaranteed.

articles.title_orig: Picture of Jane Doe shared in Snapchat group on night of alleged Cornell rape
articles.title_zh: Picture of Jane Doe shared in Snapchat group on night of alleged Cornell rape
articles.content_orig:
Editor's warning: Some of the details in this story are graphic.
Chi Phi fraternity members shared a photo of the alleged victim in the Cornell University gang rape on Snapchat the night of the alleged assault, according to social media images obtained by CBS News.
In the photo, obtained through Jane Doe's attorney, she appears to be smiling with another man.
The photo was shared in a Snapchat group with dozens of Chi Phi fraternity brothers on the night Jane Doe was allegedly assaulted at the Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell in October 2024.
Just before the photo was sent, one man wrote, "Like you can walk in and whip it out."
Right after the photo, someone in the chat asked, "Shop still open?" Another responded, "Yeah."
The alleged victim in the case, identified only as a then-20-year-old Jane Doe, has sued seven Cornell students and the university.
Two of the accused in the case were expelled, two suspended for at least two semesters, one had already graduated before any punishment could be handed down, and two were found not to be responsible for sexual misconduct, Cornell President Michael I. Kotlikoff said on Sept. 29. No one was arrested.
Two of those accused have denied responsibility through their lawyers.  Others have not shared statements.
The Tompkins County, New York, district attorney who decided not to press charges announced last month he was reopening the case in the wake of the lawsuit. Then on Thursday, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to replace Van Houten amid criticism over how the case was handled.
CBS News has obtained the findings of Cornell University's monthslong Title IX investigation into what happened that night. At a university hearing in May 2025, the then-sophomore said she "felt like bait" on the night of the alleged attack. She added, "I felt like lions around me. It just was a totally debilitating place to be in."
According to the report, she told campus investigators she took the drug ketamine and described it as feeling like the "lights are on, but nobody's home. Your brain is not functioning at its proper level."
CBS News New York also obtained hundreds of pages of interviews with Jane Doe, 20 witnesses and six of the seven men named in the lawsuit. In them, the men and Jane Doe share conflicting accounts of what happened.
Some of those men stated Jane Doe didn't appear to be intoxicated and that she gave consent. But Jane Doe describes a night that turned to horror, with multiple men coming in and out the room, stating at one point she felt "cornered," saying she "was a sex doll for all intents and purposes."
Later that night, she said was ushered into a closet by two of the men, calling it the worst experience she had the whole night, saying, "It was just raping." She said she was in and out of consciousness.
According to the Title IX investigation, one student who had been at the frat house the night of the alleged assault said she got a call the next day from one of the accused men who asked her to make sure a friend of hers didn't "say anything that she thinks might've happened last night."
In the days after the alleged assault, Jane Doe said three men apologized to her.
According to a transcript of her interview with campus investigators, she said she collected evidence, including the dress she wore that night. Two days after the alleged sexual assault, she went to a campus clinic to treat a urinary tract infection, according to her lawsuit.
Her attorney says she told doctors it was contracted in a "traumatic way," and instead of being referred for a rape kit, she was advised to "speak with somebody."
On Thursday night in a fiery town hall , Cornell students demanded change.
"Survivors need to know that when they come forward with their stories, somebody will listen and a broader institution will act upon it. Through this event, we have witnessed the complete opposite," said Jane Wang of the Cornell American Civil Liberties Union chapter.

articles.title_orig: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
articles.title_zh: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
articles.content_orig:
Spain's Congress has rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis, in a defeat for the government of Pedro Sánchez that increases pressure on him to call a snap election.
Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by the government in response to nationwide protests that have followed the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, from her home.
The decrees, which introduced a series of initiatives aimed at protecting tenants in the rental market, required parliamentary approval in order to remain in place.
MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.
Hundreds of demonstrators had gathered outside Congress as the debate took place and there were angry scenes.
Protesters chanted "shame on you" and "your profits, our misery", after the results were announced.
The government's defeat underlines the fact that Sánchez, a Socialist, does not command a congressional majority and it has heightened speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer.
Sources told Spanish media that the government would spend the weekend deciding its next step, and whether to dissolve parliament.
Sánchez's beleaguered government had already been mired in a series of scandals and judicial cases affecting his Socialist Party and close allies.
Abascal was evicted after she was unable to pay a sharp rent increase introduced by Urbagestión, the company that owned her flat in central Madrid.
Hundreds of protesters gathered to oppose the eviction last week and the case triggered a broader movement across the country demanding affordable rentals, which have soared in recent years.
The social backlash has seen Urbagestión negotiate the return of Abascal to her flat on a low rent. However, protests have continued, with people occupying squares in Madrid and other cities, pitching tents in squares and with a series of marches scheduled for this weekend.
The Sindicato de Inquilinas (Tenants' Union) activist association which has been co-ordinating protests, announced during the congressional debate that it was abandoning the tent protest in central Madrid. It said it wanted to "take the struggle to all the neighbourhoods, residential blocks and homes of Madrid, wherever there are rental increases, expulsions and abuses each day, and turn the energy of the last few days into a permanent organisation".
Protesters are also calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.
The left-wing coalition government responded to the social anger by hurriedly drawing up the two decree-laws in an effort to defuse the protests.
The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".
The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Sindicato de Inquilinas .
The conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.
However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.
Friday's debate was fierce and at times angry, as supporters and opponents of the decrees clashed in Congress.
"I don't ask you, I beg you to be brave and consistent," Sánchez said, moments before the two votes took place. "Because they are not just ambitious measures, they are necessary".
He appealed to lawmakers "to put order and humanity into [the housing] market, because if we don't, it will bring down our society".
Social Affairs minister Pablo Bustinduy, of the Sumar alliance, the junior partner in the governing coalition, presented the debate in dramatic terms.
"Today is about defending an international oligarchy which is extracting the rent from salaries earned with the effort of working classes of this country in order to share it out with dividends and they don't even pay taxes in Spain," he said.
"Voting against these decrees today means defending the interests of this oligarchy and turning your back on your own people."
However, Miriam Nogueras, of JxCat, said the decrees had been hastily drawn up and lacked rigour.
She said the decrees "will allow [vulture] funds to keep buying, keep speculating and evictions to keep happening… these two decrees would provoke the opposite effect of what they aim to achieve."
The political right has argued that the government's attempts to intervene will frighten homeowners, causing them not to put their properties on the rental market and pushing prices up further.
Juan Bravo of the PP said "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

articles.title_orig: Affordable Alternatives To Apple's AirPods Max
articles.title_zh: Affordable Alternatives To Apple's AirPods Max
articles.content_orig:
If you can live without deep iOS integration and the polished design, you could save hundreds.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
If you're willing to pay for them, there's a lot to like about the AirPods Max . You get a dose of high-end design with deep iOS integration and smart features like Personalized Spatial Audio, Adaptive EQ, Live Translation, Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. There's also lossless audio over USB-C, if you're into that sort of thing, but it's more common on spec sheets these days.
Of course, the main drawback with the AirPods Max has always been the price. At $549, the headphones rank among the most expensive sets we've reviewed. But if you're willing to give up some features, namely the tools that can only be used with Apple devices, you can save a significant sum without sacrificing too much performance.
Currently being tested for review.
At $200, the Space 2 Pro will cost you less than half of a pair of the AirPods Max 2. And yes, you will need to make some sacrifices to save that much dough. First and foremost, you'll give up the deep integration with iOS and Apple devices that the AirPods Max offers. You'll also have to forego the premium design for something that's still refined, but also decidedly plastic. If neither of those are dealbreakers, then there's plenty to like about the Space 2 Pro.
This most is Anker's first Soundcore headphones with its Thus AI chip inside. The component is responsible for active noise cancellation (ANC), voice quality (on both calls and for voice controls) and HearID customized sound. The ANC setup, which also utilizes eight sensors, does a decent job with human voices and constant noise sources. Voice quality is great, thanks in part to that chip and a six-microphone configuration, but you will notice some slight degradation when the system kicks in to block background noise. And the stock tuning offers crisp highs and deep low-end tone right out of the box.
The benefit of all that plastic is the Space 2 Pro is very light, so it's comfortable to wear for extended periods of time. These headphones also have intuitive physical controls that are reliable and easy to use instead of touch panels for swipes and taps. Multipoint Bluetooth and 30 hours of battery life (ANC on) are also on the spec sheet.
$359 is still a big chunk of change, but in the case of the second-gen QuietComfort Headphones, you're paying for Bose's noise-blocking prowess. The overall sound quality here is nice too, though the company's own Ultra model does better. On these "regular" QC headphones, you get Cinema Mode and Immersive Audio, the latter of which is the company's take on spatial sound. The QuietComfort Headphones are no slouch, and you'll be plenty pleased with the performance after saving nearly $200 over the AirPods Max 2.
Read our full review here.
At this point, you've likely seen someone wearing the AirPods Max 2 during a workout. Those headphones aren't a great choice for sweaty activities since the ear pads are made of "a breathable mesh textile." Beats headphones haven't been engineered to withstand sweat either, but they were also popular among gym goers and athletes. With the Beats 360 though, Apple finally has a set of fitness headphones in its lineup with IPX4 sweat resistance.
Since Beats is owned by Apple, you get a lot of the AirPods Max benefits here. Those include one-touch pairing, automatic switching between Apple devices on your iCloud account, Audio Sharing with compatible earbuds/headphones, Find My compatibility and hands-free access to Siri. The Beats 360 lasts for up to 12 hours longer than the AirPods Max 2 (ANC enabled) and there's the ability to swap out both the ear and headband cushions. Plus, Beats' affinity for bass will help keep your energy up during a workout, but it's not as overbearing as was on the company's early models.
If you want a good set of headphones for under $100, you have to make a lot of sacrifices. However, sound quality, battery life and comfort don't have to be on that list. With Audio-Technica's M20xBT, you get a classic design and the company's warm, inviting sound quality. 60-hour battery life is excellent and the headphones are lightweight and very comfy. What you won't find here is ANC, but basics like multipoint Bluetooth and optional wired use are still available.
When the comparison device is $549, a $299 set is significantly more affordable. In this case, that's the price of the Fender Mix: a set of noise-cancelling headphones that debuted just before CES. The new line of audio devices comes from Fender Audio, a collaboration of the Fender Corporation (of guitar fame) and Riffsound. The result is a cleverly designed set of headphones with a stored lossless Bluetooth dongle and replaceable battery. There's also a crisp, detailed quality to the sound that I really enjoyed. Plus, the company now has an app for settings changes, a key element that was missing during my review.
The five-way joystick controls are pleasant to use and 52 hours of battery life with ANC enabled is a big perk. Speaking of noise cancellation, the performance is respectable here, though it's not on the level of Bose and some others. Still, it's enough to block mild-to-moderate distractions.
Skullcandy Crusher 1080: Haptic bass is the main draw here, but the ANC performance and overall audio quality don't overcome the bulky, dated design.
JBL Live 780NC: This model is comfortable to wear with lots of features and solid active noise cancellation, but the overall sound quality is underwhelming and call quality isn't great either.
Sony WH-1000XM4C: This is still a solid set of headphones six years later, but Sony's reboot doesn't offer enough to justify the $300 price tag.
Sony WH-1000XM6: The best headphones you can buy right now will only save you $99 over the AirPods Max 2. That's not nothing, but it's also not enough in our book to name it an affordable alternative.
Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd gen): This is the best ANC performance you'll find, but at $449, these headphones don't fit the description of an affordable alternative either.
Sennheiser HDB 630: I really like the sound quality on these headphones, especially with the lossless audio capabilities. But at $500, these don't offer much savings over the AirPods Max 2.
Sennheiser Momentum 5: Sennheiser's well-rounded over-ear headphones are no slouch. The main issue that kept them off of this list is the $400 price.
Sonos Ace: Sonos' original headphones are now just $350 following the debut of the Ace Ultra. But unless you also have a Sonos soundbar, these aren't a very compelling alternative for everyday use.
When Engadget compiles buyer's guides like these, we initially draw on our decades of product review expertise. Throughout each year, we review well over 100 new devices, which gives us a solid foundation for selecting the best products that fit any given criteria. For this guide specifically, I was able to revisit recently reviewed devices as a refresher, re-familiarize myself with the products on my initial short list and make the best selections based on the affordable alternatives criteria. I write almost all of the headphone reviews at Engadget, and edit those I don't write, so I have a deep knowledge of this particular category.
We may update our selections as needed, after new products are announced and reviewed.

articles.title_orig: Protests shutter hundreds of French schools as violence flares
articles.title_zh: Protests shutter hundreds of French schools as violence flares
articles.content_orig:
What’s behind France’s school protests?
Hundreds of schools have been closed across France amid a student protest movement that has turned increasingly tumultuous.
At least 400 of France’s 3,700 high schools were closed on Friday, the Ministry of National Education said, with 560 reporting protests or disruptions. The demonstrations began at high schools in the Paris area last week, but they have spread nationwide and led to violent clashes with police.
On Friday, students across the country, many clad in masks, blockaded schools, lit fires in the streets, and faced off with police as they rallied against large class sizes and absent teachers .
“We are 35 per class, we don’t have enough chairs in classrooms, the one-hour lunch break [is too short] for everyone to get food,” 15-year-old Kesia told the Reuters news agency in the Paris suburb of Pantin before running off as the police used tear gas.
Fire damaged the entrances of two high schools in the capital, Leonard de Vinci in the south of the city and Gaston-Bachelard in the southeast, with the fire brigade called to extinguish the blazes.
Students waved placards reading “We have a future to build, not to endure.”
The school protest movement coincides with a public sector strike against the government’s budget plans, raising the pressure on President Emmanuel Macron before elections next year.
Approximately 2,000 people have been detained so far, the vast majority of whom are children, according to Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin.
Parents should be liable for damage caused by their children and “pay for repairs”, he told RTL.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray warned parents to “tell their children not to go” to the protests.
At least 170 students have been wounded, along with 65 school staff members, including 40 principals, he told BFMTV. More than 100 high schools have sustained “severe damage”.
“What matters now is ensuring our children are no longer out on the streets, because they are in danger,” Geffray declared.
Rights group Amnesty International wrote on social media that “the images of high school students being assaulted by law enforcement are extremely alarming”.
“Many are minors, children,” the organisation said. “They must be protected, not beaten with batons.”
Lola, a 16-year-old speaking to the AFP news agency in the western city of Rennes, condemned what she described as police violence while standing outside Jean-Mace high school.
“It makes us even angrier – the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us,” Lola said.
The government has accused the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of commandeering the movement. Senior LFI official Manuel Bompard dismissed the assertion as a “conspiracy theory”.
In an effort to quell tensions, Geffray said he planned to meet on Friday with education unions and student associations to find room for dialogue.

articles.title_orig: Gino’s Pizza Place owner is old guard in a new world
articles.title_zh: Gino’s Pizza Place owner is old guard in a new world
articles.content_orig:
Gino has proudly served the Tonawanda community from 351 Fries Road since opening his doors in 1983.
Now in his fourth decade of making pizza at his eponymous restaurant in Tonawanda, Gino Pinzone is a part of the old guard who made Buffalo pizza a thing. At seventy years old, he still gets behind the counter of Gino’s Pizza Place at 9 a.m. to make dough, prep sauce, and mentor a new generation of employees.
You’ve been a fixture in the local food scene for decades. Where did that passion for cooking begin?
Everything started back in Sicily. My mother had eleven children, so she worked at home day and night, night and day, constantly cooking for fourteen people. I’m number eight, so I did a lot of helping, making everything you could possibly make at home. I still do it for myself today. I learned everything from her.
Did she teach you to bake?
In those days, we really could not afford meat. Bread was everything. Chinese people use rice. Mexicans use tortilla shells. We were heavy on bread. When it came out of the oven, it was a treat just to put extra virgin olive oil and black pepper on it. That was it.
How did you end up owning a pizzeria?
I went to Buffalo State for Industrial Arts; I was going to be a teacher. But in 1978, my older brother opened a pizzeria and asked me and my brother Frank to work for him. I liked it a lot. I never finished my master's degree in teaching because I was doing okay making pizzas with my brother! I opened my first solo place in November 1983, and here I am today.
What do you love the most?
My employees. Some started as high school students from across the street. They start folding boxes and then, little by little, I teach them how to do a few things here and there. They might go away for college, but they always come back. It’s rewarding. Take care of the employees because the employees will always take care of you. And that’s what they do. I trust them, and they do a great job.
It sounds almost like a family atmosphere .
I get kids coming in who might be a little quiet or shy. Their parents ask if I can hire them, to get them out of their bedrooms and away from the video games. Next thing you know, they’re hopping around and working and loving it. I tell them, “You’re learning a skill.”
It’s not just about making pizzas but also learning how to get around a restaurant. You need to do dishes, you need to cut celery, you need to do this... Even if they graduate and get a degree, they can go anywhere in the world and work in a pizzeria because they know how a kitchen moves.
Many of the restaurant’s Instagram reels feature you. Do you enjoy being in the spotlight?
[Laughs] My son Phil does all that! He puts the camera in my face and says, “Dad, we’re introducing eggplant pizza today.” I always tell him, “Phil, I’m not doing a second take.” Whatever comes out of me, comes out. We did one video recently that had 20,000 viewers. People come in now just because they want to see me and talk to me.
Why have you never expanded to a second location?
I want to be totally responsible for everything that comes out of the place. I do all the prep work. I’m there from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. every day. On Fridays, I’m there until dinner is over. On Sundays, I’m there until the Bills game is over.  Nobody does it like the owner. It’s hard to train somebody to do things the way I do. Nowadays, people open five places and there’s no personal feeling.
And after forty years, most people would be taking it easy. What keeps you coming back every morning?
It’s not the money. It’s the DNA of a pizza guy in me. I see regulars who came in as kids now bringing their own grandkids in and putting them up on my counter. Why would I walk away? It makes it all worthwhile.
